excerpts: Docling-Graph turns documents into validated **Pydantic** objects, then builds a **directed knowledge graph** with explicit semantic relationships.
**✍🏻 Input formats:** [Docling](https://docling-project.github.io/docling/usage/supported_formats/) ’s supported inputs: PDF, images, DocLang, markdown, Office and more.
Templates define both the **extraction schema** and the resulting **graph structure** .

**💎 Graphs:** Pydantic to [NetworkX](https://docling-project.github.io/docling-graph/fundamentals/graph-management/graph-conversion/) directed graphs with stable IDs, edge and [provenance](https://docling-project.github.io/docling-graph/fundamentals/graph-management/provenance/) metadata.

Every node above also carries a deterministic `__provenance__` attribute by default ( `provenance="standard"` ), pointing back to the source chunk and page it was extracted from — no extra LLM calls involved.
**📍 Data grounding:** Deterministic [provenance](https://docling-project.github.io/docling-graph/fundamentals/graph-management/provenance/) ledger with bounding-box geometry and no extra LLM calls.

This transformation enables high-precision use cases in **chemistry, finance, and legal** domains, where AI must capture exact entity connections (compounds and reactions, instruments and dependencies, properties and measurements) **rather than rely on approximate text embeddings** .

This toolkit supports two extraction paths: **local VLM extraction** via Docling, and **LLM-based extraction** routed through **LiteLLM** for local runtimes (vLLM, Ollama) and API providers (OpenAI, Gemini, IBM watsonx, Mistral and more), all orchestrated through a flexible, config-driven pipeline.

excerpts: Granite Docling is a multimodal Image-Text-to-Text model engineered for efficient document conversion.
**Model type** : Multi-modal model (image+text-to-text)

**Model Summary** : Granite Docling 258M builds upon the Idefics3 architecture, but introduces two key modifications: it replaces the vision encoder with siglip2-base-patch16-512 and substitutes the language model with a Granite 165M LLM.

The architecture of granite-docling-258m consists of the following components: (1) Vision encoder: [siglip2-base-patch16-512](https://huggingface.co/google/siglip2-base-patch16-512) . (2) Vision-language connector: pixel shuffle projector (as in idefics3) (3) Large language model: Granite 165M. We built upon [Idefics3](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/en/model_doc/idefics3) to train our model.
granite-docling-258m

The easiest way to use this model is through the [🐥Docling](https://github.com/docling-project/docling) library. It will automatically download this model and convert documents to various formats for you.

Alternatively, you can use bare **transformers** , **vllm** , **onnx** or **mlx-vlm** to perform inference, and [docling-core](https://github.com/docling-project/docling-core) APIs to convert results to variety of output formats (md, html, etc.):

Place your page images here OUTPUT_DIR = "out/" PROMPT_TEXT = "Convert this page to docling." messages = [ { "role" : "user" , "content" : [ { "type" : "image" }, { "type" : "text" , "text" : PROMPT_TEXT}, ], }, ] Ensure output directory exists os.makedirs(OUTPUT_DIR, exist_ok= True ) Initialize LLM llm = LLM(model=MODEL_PATH, revision= "untied" , limit_mm_per_prompt={ "image" : 1 }) processor = AutoProcessor.from_pretrained(MODEL_PATH) sampling_params = SamplingParams( temperature= 0.0 , max_tokens= 8192 , skip_special_tokens= False , ) Load and prepare all images and prompts up front batched_inputs = [] image_names = [] for img_file in sorted (os.listdir(IMAGE_DIR)): if img_file.lower().endswith(( ".png" , ".jpg" , ".jpeg" )): img_path = os.path.join(IMAGE_DIR, img_file) with Image. open (img_path) as im: image = im.convert( "RGB" ) prompt = processor.apply_chat_template(messages, add_generation_prompt= True ) batched_inputs.append({ "prompt" : prompt, "multi_modal_data" : { "image" : image}}) image_names.append(os.path.splitext(img_file)[ 0 ]) Run batch inference start_time = time.time() outputs = llm.generate(batched_inputs, sampling_params=sampling_params) Postprocess all results for  img_fn, output, input_data  in zip (image_names, outputs, batched_inputs): doctags = output.outputs[ 0 ].text output_path_dt = Path(OUTPUT_DIR) / f" {img_fn} .dt" output_path_md = Path(OUTPUT_DIR) / f" {img_fn} . md" with open (output_path_dt, "w" , encoding= "utf-8" ) as f: f.write(doctags) Convert to DoclingDocument and save markdown doctags_doc = DocTagsDocument.from_doctags_and_image_pairs([doctags], [input_data[ "multi_modal_data" ][ "image" ]]) doc = DoclingDocument.load_from_doctags(doctags_doc, document_name= "Document" ) doc.save_as_markdown(output_path_md)

Model Support Policy At vLLM, we are committed to facilitating the integration and support of third-party models within our ecosystem. Our approach is designed to balance the need for robustness and the practical limitations of supporting a wide range of models. Here’s how we manage third-party model support: **Community-Driven Support**: We encourage community contributions for adding new models. When a user requests support for a new model, we welcome pull requests (PRs) from the community. These contributions are evaluated primarily on the sensibility of the output they generate, rather than strict consistency with existing implementations such as those in transformers. **Call for contribution:** PRs coming directly from model vendors are greatly appreciated! **Best-Effort Consistency**: While we aim to maintain a level of consistency between the models implemented in vLLM and other frameworks like transformers, complete alignment is not always feasible. Record issuance, falling costs, tighter spreads—and a slowdown in sustainable bonds: 2025 marked a year of unexpected developments in Latin American and Caribbean capital markets.
Issuance reached record levels in 2025** : Latin American and Caribbean (LAC) international bond issuance totalled US$ 187 billion, surpassing previous peaks and marking a record high (figure 1).
The increase was supported by favourable market conditions—including lower borrowing costs and a weaker U.S. dollar—as well as improved investor sentiment.

It is defined as a pydantic datatype, which can express several features common to documents, such as: Text, Tables, Pictures, and more Document hierarchy with sections and groups Disambiguation between main body and headers, footers (furniture) Layout information (i.e. bounding boxes) for all items, if available Provenance information The definition of the Pydantic types is implemented in the module `docling_core.types.doc` , more details in [source code definitions](https://github.com/docling-project/docling-core/tree/main/docling_core/types/doc) . It also brings a set of document construction APIs to build up a `DoclingDocument` from scratch.

A `DoclingDocument` exposes top-level fields for the document content, organized in two categories. The first category is the _content items_ , which are stored in these fields: `texts` : All items that have a text representation (paragraph, section heading, equation, ...). Base class is `TextItem` . `tables` : All tables, type `TableItem` . Can carry structure annotations. `pictures` : All pictures, type `PictureItem` . Can carry structure annotations. `key_value_items` : All key-value items. All of the above fields are lists and store items inheriting from the `DocItem` type. They can express different data structures depending on their type, and reference parents and children through JSON pointers. The second category is _content structure_ , which is encapsulated in: `body` : The root node of a tree-structure for the main document body `furniture` : The root node of a tree-structure for all items that don't belong into the body (headers, footers, ...) `groups` : A set of items that don't represent content, but act as containers for other content items (e.g. a list, a chapter) All of the above fields are only storing `NodeItem` instances, which reference children and parents through JSON pointers. **Model Summary** : Granite Docling 258M builds upon the Idefics3 architecture, but introduces two key modifications: it replaces the vision encoder with siglip2-base-patch16-512 and substitutes the language model with a Granite 165M LLM.

The architecture of granite-docling-258m consists of the following components: (1) Vision encoder: [siglip2-base-patch16-512](https://huggingface.co/google/siglip2-base-patch16-512) . (2) Vision-language connector: pixel shuffle projector (as in idefics3) (3) Large language model: Granite 165M. How to decide `VLLM_CPU_KVCACHE_SPACE`?[¶](#how-to-decide-vllm%5Fcpu%5Fkvcache%5Fspace "Permanent link") This value is 4GB by default. Larger space can support more concurrent requests, longer context length. However, users should take care of memory capacity of each NUMA node. The memory usage of each TP rank is the sum of `weight shard size` and `VLLM_CPU_KVCACHE_SPACE`, if it exceeds the capacity of a single NUMA node, the TP worker will be killed with `exitcode 9` due to out-of-memory.

vLLM has experimental support for s390x architecture on IBM Z platform. For now, users must build from source to natively run on IBM Z platform. Currently, the CPU implementation for s390x architecture supports FP32, BF16 and FP16.

Which `dtype` should be used?[¶](#which-dtype-should-be-used "Permanent link") Currently, vLLM CPU uses model default settings as `dtype`. However, due to unstable float16 support in torch CPU, it is recommended to explicitly set `dtype=bfloat16` if there are any performance or accuracy problem.

Rather than treating a complex document as a single monolithic task, Deep Extract deploys sub-agents to break it down and conquer each piece, which is what allows it to remain accurate even on documents with thousands of rows across hundreds of pages. The key is that you can define what correct looks like, directly in your system prompt. Without one, Deep Extract can still intelligently determine one that could suit the task the best. For an invoice, that might be: "ensure all line items sum to the stated total." For a financial statement: "verify that assets equal liabilities plus equity." Without this, the alternative is a person manually checking every field — a process that could take hours or even days depending on the length of the document. With the citations flag enabled, the output also contains granular bounding boxes for all the fields extracted. This can be incredibly powerful for audit trails, human review workflows, and any application where you need to trace an extracted value back to its exact location in the original document. What Deep Extract unlocks in real production cases Through our beta testing period, we worked closely with Reducto design partners to make sure Deep Extract was effective with real-world documents and use cases. Many of their engineering teams had tried all the other solutions on the market, but to no avail. Some other use cases included extraction from: A county’s payment report with transmittal number, check number, price, description, pay date and more Active exchange positions reports with symbol, cost basis, and unrealized gain/loss Agricultural invoices with payment details like invoice number, CHQ number/date, bill amount, deduction, net, and more Cattle sales invoices, county payment approval reports, residential permit applications, and job detail reports Each line item could have 10+ columns to account for, with thousands of pages per document.

**✍🏻 Input formats:** [Docling](https://docling-project.github.io/docling/usage/supported_formats/) ’s supported inputs: PDF, images, DocLang, markdown, Office and more.
Templates define both the **extraction schema** and the resulting **graph structure** .

**💎 Graphs:** Pydantic to [NetworkX](https://docling-project.github.io/docling-graph/fundamentals/graph-management/graph-conversion/) directed graphs with stable IDs, edge and [provenance](https://docling-project.github.io/docling-graph/fundamentals/graph-management/provenance/) metadata.

Every node above also carries a deterministic `__provenance__` attribute by default ( `provenance="standard"` ), pointing back to the source chunk and page it was extracted from — no extra LLM calls involved.
**📍 Data grounding:** Deterministic [provenance](https://docling-project.github.io/docling-graph/fundamentals/graph-management/provenance/) ledger with bounding-box geometry and no extra LLM calls.

Our approach is designed to balance the need for robustness and the practical limitations of supporting a wide range of models. Here’s how we manage third-party model support: **Community-Driven Support**: We encourage community contributions for adding new models. When a user requests support for a new model, we welcome pull requests (PRs) from the community. These contributions are evaluated primarily on the sensibility of the output they generate, rather than strict consistency with existing implementations such as those in transformers. **Call for contribution:** PRs coming directly from model vendors are greatly appreciated! **Best-Effort Consistency**: While we aim to maintain a level of consistency between the models implemented in vLLM and other frameworks like transformers, complete alignment is not always feasible. any linear that is neither fused nor named in the plan is replicated. `base_model_pp_plan` is a `dict` that maps direct child layer names to `tuple`s of `list`s of `str`s: You only need to do this for layers which are not present on all pipeline stages vLLM assumes that there will be only one `nn.ModuleList`, which is distributed across the pipeline stages When no `base_model_pp_plan` is provided, the Transformers modelling backend infers the split from the text model's sole `nn.ModuleList`, keeping the parameter-bearing modules around it (input embeddings, final norm) on the first/last stage (depending on declaration order) and parameter-free modules (e.g. rotary embeddings) on every stage The `list` in the first element of the `tuple` contains the names of the input arguments

content.executive_summary:
- **Parser Moat**: Docling officially supports diverse formats, advanced PDF layout, reading order, table structure, formulas, OCR, a unified document representation, and XBRL financial reports [executive_summary[0]] [6]. -> Make Docling the canonical ingest layer and treat plain PDF-to-text as a test baseline only.
- **Service Boundary**: Docling Serve runs Docling as an API, exposes API documentation and a UI, and demonstrates a `/v1/convert/source` endpoint [executive_summary[1]] [28]. -> Put parsing behind a queue and HTTP boundary so LedgerLens can swap models without rewriting its product.
- **Dual Retrieval**: Docling Graph turns documents into validated Pydantic objects and directed graphs with semantic relationships; its stated finance and legal use cases target exact entity connections rather than approximate text embeddings [executive_summary[2]] [15]. -> Ship vector retrieval plus a narrow, schema-first graph, not vector-only RAG.
- **Provenance First**: Docling Graph maps nodes to source chunks and pages, and its grounding ledger is built from pipeline bookkeeping without an extra LLM call. -> Store page, chunk, source hash, model version, and validation state for every extracted fact.
- **Hardware Reality**: Granite-Docling is a compact **258M** model derived from Idefics3 [executive_summary[3]] [36], but the current vLLM supported-models evidence does not explicitly list Granite-Docling [executive_summary[4]] [9]. -> On the 32GB APU, run classic parsing locally and use a remote LLM/VLM; make local VLM serving an experiment, not a demo dependency.
- **Commercial Benchmark**: Reducto combines custom and frontier models for citation-ready outputs across **30+ file types** [executive_summary[5]] [31]. Its Deep Extract loop extracts, verifies against the source, corrects inconsistencies, and can emit granular bounding boxes [executive_summary[6]] [11]. -> Borrow the verification and citation UX, but compete on LATAM filing coverage and longitudinal comparability.
- **Market Timing**: CEPAL reports **US$187 billion** of Latin American and Caribbean international bond issuance in 2025, record high, while spreads narrowed **131 basis points** to **330 basis points** at year-end [executive_summary[7]] [17]. -> Position LedgerLens as disclosure intelligence for an active market, not as a generic chatbot.
- **Proof of Need**: The Evident 2026 LATAM index ranks **20** banks across Transparency, Leadership, Innovation, and Talent; none had shared realized or projected ROI across all AI activities at publication [executive_summary[8]] [8]. -> Make auditability, measurable analyst time saved, and traceable answers the thought-leadership wedge.
content.the_2026_architecture_decision_evidence_:
The recommendation is a hybrid, evidence-first pipeline:

```text
Regulator / issuer sources
        |
        v
Source adapters -> immutable raw files + metadata + source hash
        |
        v
Docling worker or docling-serve -> DoclingDocument
        |
        +--> structured/XBRL lane -> normalized facts and time series
        |
        +--> HybridChunker -> vector index for narrative discovery
        |
        +--> narrow Pydantic extraction -> graph and evidence ledger
        |
        v
Hybrid retriever -> validator -> answer composer -> page/box citations
```

Docling's unified representation is a Pydantic datatype that can carry text, tables, pictures, hierarchy, layout information, and provenance [the_2026_architecture_decision_evidence_before_agents[0]] [12]. Its official project also lists XBRL financial reports as an application-specific input [the_2026_architecture_decision_evidence_before_agents[1]] [6]. That makes it a better system boundary for LedgerLens than storing only flattened Markdown: the product can retain both the reading structure and the original source coordinates.

| Layer | Ship now | Defer until evidence exists | Decision rationale |
|---|---|---|---|
| Source coverage | Start with one regulator-grade adapter, such as Chile's CMF Hechos Esenciales, plus issuer PDF and XBRL ingestion where available. | Add country-specific adapters one by one. | CMF already exposes a searchable material-event corpus with entity and date filters [the_2026_architecture_decision_evidence_before_agents[2]] [26]. Country adapters are a product moat, not plumbing. |
| Parsing | Docling library in batch workers; docling-serve for a stable HTTP boundary. | Alternate VLM parsers and commercial fallbacks. | Docling Serve supports package or container deployment and returns conversion results through an API [the_2026_architecture_decision_evidence_before_agents[3]] [28]. |
| Retrieval | HybridChunker for structure-aware chunks, a vector index for narrative text, and relational storage for normalized facts. | A graph for every extracted sentence. | Docling's chunkers preserve hierarchy and can repeat table headers when a table spans chunks [the_2026_architecture_decision_evidence_before_agents[4]] [20]. |
| Extraction | A small Pydantic schema for issuer, report, period, statement, metric, unit, event, risk, and source anchor. | Broad domain ontology and autonomous schema discovery. | Narrow schemas make validation and regression tests possible. |
| Graph | Feature-flag a graph for high-value financial relations and material events. | Cross-document graph expansion and unrestricted graph QA. | Docling Graph is schema-first; its templates define both extraction schema and graph structure [the_2026_architecture_decision_evidence_before_agents[5]] [15]. |
| Models | Remote OpenAI-compatible LLM endpoint through LiteLLM for extraction; CPU-friendly embeddings on the demo PC. | Local Granite-Docling VLM and local large LLM. | Docling Graph supports LLM extraction through LiteLLM [the_2026_architecture_decision_evidence_before_agents[5]] [15], while the APU does not establish a safe local VLM path. |
| Trust layer | Store field-level provenance, validation status, confidence, and a clickable source excerpt. | Agentic self-correction across every document. | The trust layer is the customer-facing product, not a later observability feature. |

The minimum viable LedgerLens answer should therefore return a value, period, currency, unit, source document, page, excerpt or box, extraction model, and validation result. A user should be able to reject a fact without trusting the model. **Decision: ship the evidence ledger and hybrid retrieval before an autonomous agent.**
content.docling_versus_naive_parsing_and_ragflow:
The comparison is not simply "which parser wins." Docling is a reusable document representation and processing toolkit; DeepDoc is a vision-plus-parser subsystem inside RAGFlow; naive parsing is a deliberately weak baseline that converts a PDF to text and chunks it without a structural contract.

| Approach | What it preserves or does | Financial-filings fit | Use in LedgerLens |
|---|---|---|---|
| Naive PDF-to-text | Fast text extraction with no guaranteed reading order, table semantics, page geometry, or field-level provenance. This is a baseline definition, not a claim about one named product. | Useful for a smoke test; unsafe as the canonical representation for tables, footnotes, and multi-column filings. | Keep only as a regression baseline and emergency fallback. |
| RAGFlow DeepDoc | Has vision and parser parts [docling_versus_naive_parsing_and_ragflow_deepdoc[0]] [34]. It recognizes text, titles, figures, captions, tables, headers, footers, references, and equations [docling_versus_naive_parsing_and_ragflow_deepdoc[0]] [34]. Its table recognizer handles hierarchy headers, spanning cells, and projected row headers, and can reassemble tables into LLM-readable sentences [docling_versus_naive_parsing_and_ragflow_deepdoc[0]] [34]. | Strong candidate when the priority is a ready-made RAG workflow and visual chunk inspection. | Benchmark it against Docling on a fixed filing set; use RAGFlow optionally, not as a dependency. |
| Docling classic | Supports advanced PDF layout, reading order, table structure, formulas, OCR, multiple formats, unified DoclingDocument, and XBRL financial reports [docling_versus_naive_parsing_and_ragflow_deepdoc[1]] [6]. | Best foundation for preserving a stable intermediate representation and adding structured extraction later. | Use as the canonical parser and expose it through docling-serve. |

DeepDoc is more capable than a naive parser, especially for scanned or rotated tables. Its PDF parser can output positioned text chunks, tables with cropped images and natural-language content, and figures with captions and figure text [docling_versus_naive_parsing_and_ragflow_deepdoc[0]] [34]. That is valuable for RAG, but the output is still a RAG-oriented parsing path. Docling gives LedgerLens a broader interchange layer: the same document can feed Markdown or JSON export, hierarchical chunking, structured extraction, and a future graph [docling_versus_naive_parsing_and_ragflow_deepdoc[1]] [6][docling_versus_naive_parsing_and_ragflow_deepdoc[2]] [5].

The failure case is important. A table converted into prose may answer a simple question but lose row-column identity, units, or repeated headers when retrieved out of context. Conversely, a perfect layout representation does not guarantee correct financial interpretation. LedgerLens therefore needs parser tests for reading order, table structure, footnotes, rotated scans, and currency/unit retention, followed by semantic validation. **Decision: use Docling as the source of truth, DeepDoc as an optional benchmark or RAGFlow integration, and naive parsing only to quantify the cost of losing structure.**
content.docling_graph_versus_vector_only_rag:
Vector retrieval is the right default for open-ended discovery: "find the discussion of liquidity risk" or "retrieve the paragraphs about a restructuring." It is weaker for exact relations such as issuer -> metric -> period -> value, or event -> affected instrument -> date. Docling Graph's own positioning is explicit: it targets exact entity connections in finance and legal contexts rather than relying on approximate text embeddings [docling_graph_versus_vector_only_rag[0]] [15].

Docling Graph uses templates to define both the extraction schema and graph structure, validates the result as Pydantic objects, and converts those objects into directed NetworkX graphs with stable IDs, edge metadata, and provenance [docling_graph_versus_vector_only_rag[0]] [15]. Its two stated extraction paths are local VLM extraction through Docling and LLM extraction through LiteLLM [docling_graph_versus_vector_only_rag[0]] [15]. This is enough to support a practical hybrid design without claiming that every document needs a graph.

| Query type | Vector-only RAG | Graph or structured lane | LedgerLens answer path |
|---|---|---|---|
| Narrative discovery | Strong semantic recall when chunks are good. | Often unnecessary overhead. | Vector search, reranking, then cited passages. |
| Exact KPI by period | Can retrieve the right paragraph but may mix periods, units, or tables. | Validated fields and period-aware edges. | Structured lookup first, vector evidence second. |
| Material-event change | Can find similar language but does not inherently model event identity or chronology. | Event nodes, issuer edges, dates, and source anchors. | Graph filter plus source excerpt. |
| Cross-issuer comparison | Requires careful query-time normalization. | Normalized entities, units, and relationships. | Graph or relational query plus the original documents. |
| New document type | No schema work, but quality depends on parsing and retrieval. | Requires schema and validation work. | Start vector-first, promote high-value fields into schemas. |

The provenance benefit is not merely a citation string. Docling Graph says its deterministic grounding maps graph nodes to source chunks and pages; the detailed reference describes chunk IDs, page numbers, document-item references, and optional source-anchor spans [docling_graph_versus_vector_only_rag[1]] [14]. The high-level README also advertises bounding-box geometry [docling_graph_versus_vector_only_rag[0]] [15]. The safe product promise is therefore: every promoted fact has a source anchor, while the exact availability of a box should be tested per parser and document type.

The limitation is schema cost and extraction uncertainty. Deterministic grounding does not make a hallucinated value correct; it only makes the value auditable. A graph should be promoted when LedgerLens has a repeated question, a stable field definition, and a validation rule. **Decision: ship a narrow graph for high-value facts and events, while keeping vector retrieval as the recall layer.**
content.granite_docling_vllm_ragflow_and_the_32g:
There are three separate questions: whether vLLM serves VLMs in general, whether it serves Granite-Docling specifically, and whether the demo PC can run the combination acceptably.

| Runtime path | Evidence-based verdict | Recommendation for LedgerLens |
|---|---|---|
| vLLM as a serving layer | vLLM provides an OpenAI-compatible API and documents support for NVIDIA GPUs, AMD GPUs, CPUs, and other hardware plugins [granite_docling_vllm_ragflow_and_the_32gb_apu[0]] [16]. | Use it later as a model-serving boundary for a supported model. |
| vLLM plus Granite-Docling | Granite-Docling is a **258M** model based on Idefics3, with a SigLIP2 vision encoder and Granite 165M language model [granite_docling_vllm_ragflow_and_the_32gb_apu[1]] [36]. The current supported-models evidence does not explicitly list Granite-Docling [granite_docling_vllm_ragflow_and_the_32gb_apu[2]] [9]. | Treat direct vLLM serving as an integration experiment, not a production capability claim. |
| vLLM for Docling Graph LLM extraction | Docling Graph routes LLM extraction through LiteLLM [granite_docling_vllm_ragflow_and_the_32gb_apu[3]] [15], and vLLM exposes an OpenAI-compatible API [granite_docling_vllm_ragflow_and_the_32gb_apu[0]] [16]. | Feasible in principle for a compatible text model; test structured output, tool use, context, and failure recovery before depending on it. |
| CPU inference on the demo PC | vLLM documents basic CPU inference and serving; its x86 guidance calls for `avx512f` recommended or `avx2` with limited features, and AMD CPU execution requires at least Zen 4/Genoa for AVX512 [granite_docling_vllm_ragflow_and_the_32gb_apu[4]] [27]. | Use CPU vLLM only for a small text model if the exact CPU qualifies. Do not promise local VLM throughput. |
| AMD GPU / APU path | vLLM documents ROCm support and lists specific AMD families, including MI-series cards, Radeon RX 7900/9000, and Ryzen AI MAX / AI 300 Series; the latter requires ROCm 7.0.2 or above in the cited guidance [granite_docling_vllm_ragflow_and_the_32gb_apu[5]] [32]. | Check the exact APU SKU, Linux environment, ROCm version, and memory behavior. Generic "32GB APU" is not a supported hardware guarantee. |
| Granite-Docling MLX | The MLX conversion is optimized for Apple Silicon Macs and is converted from Granite-Docling 258M using mlx-vlm [granite_docling_vllm_ragflow_and_the_32gb_apu[6]] [33]. | Not a solution for an AMD APU. |
| RAGFlow vLLM factory | The current `rag/llm` directory listing shows chat, embedding, OCR, reranking, sequence-to-text, tool, and TTS modules, but the cited source does not show a vLLM factory, vLLM class, or configuration [granite_docling_vllm_ragflow_and_the_32gb_apu[7]] [25]. | Pin the exact RAGFlow release and inspect its code before making it a dependency. Use RAGFlow as an optional workflow/UI benchmark. |

The demo plan is straightforward: run Docling and docling-serve locally, keep raw files and rendered page evidence local, call a remote extraction model through LiteLLM, and cache results. If the exact APU is a documented Ryzen AI MAX or AI 300 configuration, test ROCm separately, but do not make the demo depend on it. The 258M parameter count is encouraging, but the evidence does not establish a 32GB memory requirement, VLM latency, or reliable integrated-GPU performance.

RAGFlow remains useful as a reference implementation. Its public material describes configurable LLM and embedding models, multiple recall and reranking, APIs, visual chunk intervention, and traceable citations [granite_docling_vllm_ragflow_and_the_32gb_apu[8]] [35]. It also lists Docling as a supported parsing method [granite_docling_vllm_ragflow_and_the_32gb_apu[8]] [35]. That makes it a good benchmark for workflow ergonomics, not evidence that a particular RAGFlow vLLM factory is available. **Decision: CPU-first demo, remote LLM extraction, optional RAGFlow comparison, and GPU/VLM serving only after a reproducible hardware test.**
content.reducto_borrow_the_verification_loop_bea:
Reducto is the commercial narrative LedgerLens should study, not copy literally. Its homepage positions the platform as a complete agentic document system for parsing, extracting, splitting, classifying, and editing, combining custom and frontier models for citation-ready results across **30+ file types** [reducto_borrow_the_verification_loop_beat_it_on_latam_evidence[0]] [31]. A technical Reducto page describes a hybrid agentic architecture that orchestrates multiple models across document-processing components [reducto_borrow_the_verification_loop_beat_it_on_latam_evidence[1]] [2].

The strongest idea is Deep Extract. In the April 6, 2026 announcement, Reducto describes an agent harness that verifies and corrects its own output [reducto_borrow_the_verification_loop_beat_it_on_latam_evidence[2]] [11]. The loop extracts, checks the result against the source, identifies missing or inconsistent information, and re-extracts until a defined quality threshold is met [reducto_borrow_the_verification_loop_beat_it_on_latam_evidence[2]] [11]. Its financial-statement example verifies that assets equal liabilities plus equity, and its citation flag can return granular bounding boxes for extracted fields [reducto_borrow_the_verification_loop_beat_it_on_latam_evidence[2]] [11]. That is a directly reusable LedgerLens pattern: extraction should be a hypothesis, validation should be a first-class step, and the user should see the evidence.

The 10-K point needs discipline. The Deep Extract announcement reviewed here does not list a 10-K example [reducto_borrow_the_verification_loop_beat_it_on_latam_evidence[2]] [11]. Reducto's benchmark post reports **100% completeness, 99.6% precision, 99.6% recall, and 99.3% leaf accuracy**, but the page does not provide the dataset/task description and does not state independent verification in the extracted evidence [reducto_borrow_the_verification_loop_beat_it_on_latam_evidence[3]] [37]. LedgerLens should therefore say "Reducto demonstrates an agentic extraction narrative" rather than assert that Reducto has publicly proven a specific 10-K workflow.

| Reducto playbook | Borrow | LedgerLens differentiation |
|---|---|---|
| Agentic extract-verify-correct loop [reducto_borrow_the_verification_loop_beat_it_on_latam_evidence[2]] [11] | Add deterministic checks for balance-sheet identity, period, currency, sign, and unit. | Make validation rules visible and domain-specific for EEFF and material events. |

**Case study - Reducto.** Reducto's decision is to turn extraction into an agentic quality loop instead of a single model call. The outcome it advertises is not merely JSON; it is JSON with verification and granular source locations. The mechanism reveals what enterprise buyers pay for: reduced review risk and a shorter path from a field to the document.

LedgerLens should borrow that mechanism but choose a narrower arena. A transparent benchmark across local EEFF, scanned tables, footnotes, and material-event notices can beat a broad platform on relevance even if it cannot beat it on file-type breadth. **Decision: compete on auditable LATAM disclosure workflows, not on generic parser breadth or an unverified 10-K claim.**
content.latam_current_thesis_and_future_thesis:
The current thesis is that LedgerLens should sell an evidence and comparison layer over a growing, already-public disclosure stream. CEPAL reports that international bond issuance in Latin America and the Caribbean reached a record **US$187 billion** in 2025 [latam_current_thesis_and_future_thesis[0]] [17]. The same review reports GSSS issuance of **US$17.6 billion**, equal to **9.4%** of total international issuance, after a **47%** contraction in thematic-bond activity [latam_current_thesis_and_future_thesis[0]] [17]. It also reports **35** sovereign rating actions, net positive by **11**, a **131-basis-point** narrowing in the Latin EMBIG, and year-end spreads of **330 basis points** [latam_current_thesis_and_future_thesis[0]] [17]. The MSCI Latin America Index rose **46%**, compared with **31%** for MSCI Emerging Markets and **19%** for MSCI G7 [latam_current_thesis_and_future_thesis[0]] [17]. These are market conditions, not proof of product demand, but they support a practical positioning hypothesis: active issuers and investors create repeated needs for fast, comparable, source-grounded disclosure analysis.

The AI thesis is more cautious. An IIF Staff Paper published January 17, 2025 focuses on AI in LAC financial services and identifies payments, fraud prevention, access to credit, and personalized offerings as development use cases [latam_current_thesis_and_future_thesis[1]] [1]. It also warns that data frameworks and regulatory interaction can limit AI's potential [latam_current_thesis_and_future_thesis[1]] [1]. The Evident July 2026 LATAM bank index ranks **20** major banks across Transparency, Leadership, Innovation, and Talent [latam_current_thesis_and_future_thesis[2]] [8]. Brazil accounts for **7 of 20** banks, or **35%**, and those banks produced nearly half, **49%**, of use cases with reported outcomes over the previous two years, yet none had shared realized or projected ROI across all AI activities [latam_current_thesis_and_future_thesis[2]] [8]. The message is not "AI has won." It is "governed, measurable AI is still a credibility gap."

**Case study - CMF Chile.** The CMF Hechos Esenciales page is a concrete source-system example. It says the page lets users consult events that constitute an essential or relevant fact under market and insurance rules, and that the information is received and reproduced by CMF [latam_current_thesis_and_future_thesis[3]] [26]. Its covered entities include banks, insurers, brokers, funds, and securities issuers, and the search supports date ranges and recent-document filters [latam_current_thesis_and_future_thesis[3]] [26].

The product implication is clear. The current wedge is a bilingual or multilingual evidence layer: ingest EEFF and material events, normalize issuer and period metadata, detect changes, and return citations. The future wedge is a longitudinal graph that connects issuer, instrument, event, metric, risk, and source across periods and countries. That future is plausible but not guaranteed; IIF's governance warning means LedgerLens should make provenance and policy controls part of the value proposition from the beginning.

| Horizon | What the market evidence says | LedgerLens thesis | Product move |
|---|---|---|---|
| Current | Capital-market disclosure volume and market activity are material [latam_current_thesis_and_future_thesis[0]] [17]. AI adoption is visible, but ROI disclosure remains incomplete [latam_current_thesis_and_future_thesis[2]] [8]. | Buyers need faster review with evidence, not another unmeasured chatbot. | Ship cited extraction, change detection, normalized KPIs, and an analyst audit trail. |
| Future | LAC AI development is constrained by data frameworks and regulatory interaction [latam_current_thesis_and_future_thesis[1]] [1]. | Trust, comparability, and machine-readable relationships become differentiators as workflows mature. | Expand the graph, validation rules, country adapters, and reproducible evaluation. |

**Decision: lead publicly with "auditable disclosure intelligence for LATAM" now, and treat autonomous graph agents as the future roadmap rather than the current promise.**

### Post 1: "A citation is not a footnote. It is the product."

Open with a failure case: an answer gives the right number but the wrong period or unit. Then explain the Reducto mechanism: extract, verify, find inconsistency, and re-extract [three_linkedin_post_angles_with_named_sources[0]] [11]. Contrast it with the Docling Graph provenance mechanism, which binds graph nodes to source chunks and pages through pipeline bookkeeping. Close with a LedgerLens design principle: every KPI and material event should expose page evidence, extraction state, and validation result. The claim is concrete, named, and defensible without saying that any vendor has solved every filing type.

### Post 2: "The next LATAM capital-markets AI winner may own the evidence layer."

Use CEPAL's **US$187 billion** issuance figure and the **46%** MSCI Latin America performance as the opening market context [three_linkedin_post_angles_with_named_sources[1]] [17]. Then add the counterweight: Evident reports **49%** of outcome-reporting use cases came from Brazilian banks in its sample, but no bank had shared ROI across all AI activities [three_linkedin_post_angles_with_named_sources[2]] [8]. The thesis is that the opportunity is not to announce another general copilot. It is to prove time saved, source coverage, false-positive rate, and analyst acceptance on local EEFF and hechos relevantes.

### Post 3: "Stop asking vector search to be a database."

Show a simple example: "What was EBITDA in each period, in the same currency, and what event changed the risk outlook?" Explain that vector retrieval is excellent for finding relevant narrative, while Docling Graph's Pydantic schema and directed relationships are designed for exact entity connections [three_linkedin_post_angles_with_named_sources[4]] [15]. Demonstrate a hybrid answer: graph result first, cited table or paragraph second, validation third. This post can mention Docling's table-aware chunking and DeepDoc's handling of spanning cells [three_linkedin_post_angles_with_named_sources[5]] [20][three_linkedin_post_angles_with_named_sources[6]] [34].

For all three posts, avoid claiming that LedgerLens already has capabilities it has not shipped. The credible voice is "here is the architecture and the evidence standard we are building," supported by Docling, Docling Graph, Reducto, CEPAL, Evident, IIF, and CMF. **Decision: publish the evidence standard first; let the product roadmap follow the public proof.**

The major strategies differ by mechanism, scope, trade-off, and time horizon.

| Strategy | Mechanism | Scope | Main trade-off | Best LedgerLens role |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Docling classic | Structured parsing into DoclingDocument, with layout, tables, reading order, OCR, formulas, and XBRL support [synthesis_open_structure_narrow_graphs_remote_intelligence[0]] [6]. | Broad document foundation. | Requires downstream schemas and validation. | Canonical ingest now. |
| RAGFlow DeepDoc | Vision plus parser, layout components, table structure recognition, and RAG-oriented chunks [synthesis_open_structure_narrow_graphs_remote_intelligence[1]] [34]. | Complex RAG documents. | Ties more of the workflow to RAGFlow's operating model. | Benchmark or optional orchestration. |
| Docling Graph | Schema-defined Pydantic objects converted to directed graphs with provenance [synthesis_open_structure_narrow_graphs_remote_intelligence[2]] [15]. | Exact relationships in finance and legal domains. | Schema and extraction cost; not every query needs a graph. | Narrow high-value graph now, broad graph later. |
| Vector-only RAG | Embedding similarity over chunks. | Flexible narrative discovery. | Period, unit, relation, and identity errors remain query-time risks. | Recall layer, never the only evidence layer. |
| vLLM plus VLM/LLM | Model serving behind an API; exact support depends on model and hardware [synthesis_open_structure_narrow_graphs_remote_intelligence[3]] [16][synthesis_open_structure_narrow_graphs_remote_intelligence[4]] [9]. | Production inference when hardware and model are validated. | APU compatibility and Granite-Docling support are not established by the cited evidence. | Remote or later self-hosting. |
| Reducto-style commercial IDP | Multi-model parsing plus agentic verification and field citations [synthesis_open_structure_narrow_graphs_remote_intelligence[5]] [31][synthesis_open_structure_narrow_graphs_remote_intelligence[6]] [11]. | Broad enterprise document workflows. | Vendor dependence and less local domain specialization. | UX and evaluation benchmark to borrow. |

The non-obvious tension is that the smallest attractive model, Granite-Docling at **258M**, is not automatically the easiest product dependency: model size does not settle serving support, VLM latency, or APU memory behavior [synthesis_open_structure_narrow_graphs_remote_intelligence[7]] [36][synthesis_open_structure_narrow_graphs_remote_intelligence[4]] [9]. A second tension is that a graph creates more certainty only when its schema and validation rules are narrower than the source universe. A third is market-facing: LATAM AI adoption is real enough to measure, but ROI and governance evidence are incomplete [synthesis_open_structure_narrow_graphs_remote_intelligence[8]] [8][synthesis_open_structure_narrow_graphs_remote_intelligence[9]] [1]. That makes overclaiming a competitive risk.

The resulting roadmap has three gates. First, ship Docling ingestion, source adapters, structure-aware chunks, hybrid retrieval, field-level citations, and deterministic validation. Second, promote the most repeated KPI and event questions into Docling Graph schemas and publish an evaluation set. Third, test Granite-Docling and vLLM on a known GPU or a documented AMD configuration, and only then offer self-hosted VLM extraction. This sequence keeps the demo reliable while preserving an upgrade path to local inference and agentic workflows.

**Final recommendation:** LedgerLens should be an evidence system with RAG, not a RAG system with citations added afterward. Ship the parser, provenance, validation, and hybrid retrieval now. Ship broad graph reasoning, local VLM serving, RAGFlow coupling, and a Reducto-style autonomous correction loop only after the narrow workflow has measurable accuracy and analyst value.
